display.title: Tashlich and Teshuvah: Throwing Our Sins Away Before Yom Kippur
display.summary_short: Why we say Tashlich by flowing water, and how the mitzvah of teshuvah, together with tefillah and tzedakah, gives us a clean start before Yom Kippur.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, broadcast just before Yom Kippur. Uncle Yossi reminds children of Tashlich on Rosh Hashanah and asks why it is said by a river, lake or ocean instead of in shul. If you drop something on the floor or even throw it far away, you can still go and pick it up; but whatever you throw into flowing water is carried away for good. Tashlich, named for the verse 'You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea', shows Hashem that we truly regret our mistakes and never want them back. The order of the day for every soldier in Tzivos Hashem is the mitzvah of teshuvah: daven better, say brachos slowly and carefully, give more tzedakah and respect parents, teachers and elders. Uncle Yossi closes with the Rebbe's call to begin the year with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah, all done with simcha, because Hashem, the King in the field, is close to us these days.
display.lesson: Real teshuvah means letting go of our mistakes for good, and doing more mitzvos with joy.
